items.prompt: Seed 42, move 1: cell D jogs right and the wall stops it at x = 9. The wires get 3 longer (HPWL 52 → 55) and T is 3. What is the chance that the move is accepted?
items.explain: p = e^(−Δ/T) = e^(−3/3) = 0.3679. The run draws u = 0.1748, which is below 0.3679, so the move is accepted. Only a move that is not worse (Δ ≤ 0) is accepted for sure.

items.prompt: A move with Δ = 0 (no net box changes) must pass the random test, so it uses a random number like a worsening move.
items.explain: Δ ≤ 0 is accepted without drawing anything. Seed 42 draws 4 × 60 + 25 = 265 numbers: four per move plus one for each of the 25 worsening proposals. A port that accepts only Δ < 0 draws on every Δ = 0 move and gets 35.393 instead of 49.576.

items.prompt: Seed 42 accepts 44 of its 60 moves. How many of those 44 made the HPWL smaller?
items.explain: 11 shortened the wires, 9 lengthened them (accepted by the dice) and 24 changed nothing (free moves, Δ = 0): 11 + 9 + 24 = 44. The 16 rejected moves were all among the 25 worsening proposals. Accepted is not progress.

items.prompt: A move that makes the wires 0.5 longer: what is the chance of accepting it at the start (T = 3) and at the end of the 60 moves (T = 0.0732)?
choices: 0.85 at the start, 0.001 at the end
0.85 at the start, 0.85 at the end
0.37 at the start, 0.001 at the end
1 at the start, 0 at the end
items.explain: e^(−0.5/3) = 0.8465 and e^(−0.5/0.0732) = 0.0011. T falls by a factor 0.94 after every move (3 × 0.94^60 = 0.0732), so the same worsening is almost always taken at first and almost never at the end.

items.prompt: Seed 199 accepts 37 moves, none of which ever gets below the start (52), and the last placement has HPWL 53.871. What does sa_place return?
choices: An error: the run found nothing
items.explain: The function returns the best placement seen, and the best is the start (a new best needs cur < best strictly). The final placement is 1.871 worse than the start. Seed 162 is the mild case: best 27.753 at move 59, final 27.887.

items.prompt: Seed 42 gives 49.6, so on this instance a 60-move annealing run is expected to end near 49.6.
items.explain: Seed 42 is the third-worst of seeds 1 to 200. 197 of the 200 seeds do better; the best values go from 13.729 (seed 134) to 52.000 (seed 199) with a median of 36.043. One seed is one story: judge a random method by many runs.

items.prompt: 300 moves on seed 42 reach HPWL 2.612, far below the "golden" placement of 14. Why is that not a better placement?
choices: The annealer is broken: HPWL cannot go below 14
HPWL has no overlap rule, so the cells pile up (A, B, C, D end within 0.5 of each other; bin overflow 4 against 2 at the start)
300 moves are too few for the result to count
The 2.612 comes from the final placement, not the best one
items.explain: Nothing in the cost keeps cells apart: six cells on one point would give HPWL 0 (bin overflow 5). So 14 is not a floor and a low HPWL alone is not a good placement. A density term, the next module, is the missing piece.

items.prompt: tiny_place.json lists A and D as fixed pads, so in this lab's annealer cells A and D never move.
items.explain: This annealer moves every cell. On seed 42, 20 of the 60 proposals are on A or D and 17 are accepted: A ends at (0, 1.99) and D at (5.76, 9). Freezing them (--freeze A,D, an experiment) gives 51.096 instead of 49.576.
